decisions.decision: Static source scanners are defense-in-depth; runtime/data invariants carry the correctness guarantee
decisions.rationale: Three review rounds in Phase 3 each closed the reviewer's exact reproduction and the next reviewer found another spelling. Convergence came only after declaring the data gates load-bearing. The user later asked for the static classes to be closed anyway, and they were -- but the ordering stands.

decisions.decision: Battery sleep is held by a LaunchDaemon, not a one-shot command
decisions.rationale: `pmset -b disablesleep 1` applied by hand on 09-17 had reset itself to 0 by 09-19 with no reboot; 14.17h of irreplaceable L1 was lost over 34 outages in three days. The daemon re-asserts every 300s. Proved: flipped to 0, restored after ~195s.

decisions.decision: The feature tier refuses a held-out date at BOTH the write and the read, and the refusal covers day D when D+1 is held out
decisions.rationale: Day D's 10-minute label tail stores D+1's prevailing mids; `mid_t * (1 + ret_10min_mid)` reconstructs them to 1.5e-11 USDT. Without the D+1 rule the feature tier would hand back exactly what the lockbox withholds.

decisions.decision: trade_flow accumulates in int64, not float64
decisions.rationale: With a float64 running sum, changing the same-etime tie order changes trade_flow on 95% of decision rows (float addition is not associative). In int64 the result is bit-identical under either tie order, so reproducibility stops depending on the merge convention. int64 also measured 6% faster.

decisions.decision: Label staleness is bounded by the horizon itself (no quote in (t, t+h]), not by one absolute 30s threshold
decisions.rationale: One absolute threshold served horizons of 1s and 10s alike, so a silence up to 3x the primary horizon produced a finite 0.0 from a carried-forward price. The horizon-relative bound needs no config and avoids the opposite error a per-horizon table introduces.

decisions.decision: Every invariance property needs an anti-vacuity counterpart
decisions.rationale: A constant-returning feature passes both shuffle-invariance properties -- a constant genuinely cannot see the future. Only a sensitivity assertion catches the stub.
